headline: High: Langflow’s default server-side, unsandboxed flow execution can amplify shared-workspace leakage and cascading errors when paired with a local game agent, while prompt-injection risk is limited by the game agent’s lack of I/O surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: godot_rl_agents shows no I/O surfaces and no network egress, so it cannot ingest Langflow output by default. Langflow can chain agents and wire tools, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel; the only plausible bridge is unusual manual copy/paste or deployment-specific plumbing, so injection risk stays low.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Langflow output into a prompt consumed by godot_rl_agents, injection becomes plausible.
IF a deployment adds a shared filesystem, clipboard bridge, or MCP-like channel between the two, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate hosts or containers.
Disable copy/paste handoff for untrusted Langflow outputs.
Add a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from imported text.
Log and review any manual transfer between systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Langflow reads and writes server files and uploads flow inputs/intermediate outputs, while godot_rl_agents has no documented data surfaces. If both are deployed on the same workspace, Langflow can expose files or secrets that the game agent never needed, making leakage plausible in default Langflow setups even though the pairwise bridge is indirect.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem or mounted workspace, Langflow can read files the game agent can access.
IF flow inputs include secrets or uploaded files, Langflow may transmit them to configured model providers or HTTP services.
mitigations: Place Langflow in a separate workspace with least-privilege mounts.
Store secrets outside any shared directory.
Restrict uploaded files to a dedicated quarantine folder.
Review flow components that call external APIs.
Rotate any credentials exposed to Langflow.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow has write_filesystem and broad execution capabilities, plus server-side shared state across instances; godot_rl_agents is runnable but exposes no write surface. The conflict is asymmetric, but if both touch the same directory or artifacts, Langflow can overwrite or race with the game agent’s files, so the interaction exists without a built-in lock.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, Langflow can overwrite artifacts created for godot_rl_agents.
IF multiple Langflow instances share server-side state, concurrent writes can race on shared resources.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Mount shared paths read-only where possible.
Serialize writes with an external lock file.
Disable concurrent runs on the same workspace.
Snapshot important files before running flows.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is a graph-based orchestrator that can chain multiple agents and tools, and its Python code component runs server-side unsandboxed by default. If godot_rl_agents output is fed into Langflow as authoritative input, Langflow can turn a mistaken game-state or text artifact into downstream actions or API calls, creating a dangerous cascade in default deployments.
conditions: IF godot_rl_agents output is connected to a Langflow node without verification, Langflow may act on incorrect content.
IF a Langflow flow includes external API or code nodes, a bad upstream output can trigger downstream side effects.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action node.
Add schema validation between the agents.
Disable code nodes for untrusted inputs.
Require explicit allowlists for downstream tools.
Run the flow in a staging environment first.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented for godot_rl_agents, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and processes flow inputs/intermediate outputs. The only compliance concern visible here is generic handling of secrets and logs, so this is a low-risk overlap rather than a residency or regulated-data breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Langflow flows, its storage and logging settings become compliance-relevant.
IF deployment policy requires residency controls, Langflow must be configured to meet them.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in flows.
Review Langflow retention and logging settings.
Store credentials in an external secret manager.
Document the data classes allowed in each flow.
Use a deployment region that matches policy.
